# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the actual network through `view.model`, alongside training histories and metadata references. It resolves the model’s `sample_batch` function to obtain corruption bookkeeping when available.

The margin probe consumes up to ten `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` batches with matching B × L shapes. It validates token ranges, computes sequence features, and scores stacked positive/negative items, requiring B × L × 2 logits. Feature probes run in evaluation mode without gradients and restore the previous training mode.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Directional alignment:** Samples up to 2,048 real-item embeddings, excluding padding/MASK, and maps mean pairwise cosine to [0,1]. Higher values indicate stronger alignment, not conclusive collapse.
- **Representation geometry:** Samples up to 256 items and users; reports raw norms, centered variance, singular values, and RankMe effective rank. Very low variance/rank can flag limited representation spread; larger values alone do not establish recommendation quality.
- **Positive–negative margins:** Reports mean, tenth percentile, negative-win rate, and fraction below 0.5 over valid supervised positions. Larger margins and lower failure rates indicate clearer sampled-item separation.
- **Coverage and allocation:** Counts valid targets, terminal targets, observed input types, and empty batches. Exact corruption branches are counted only when sampler bookkeeping matches all batch arrays. Optional training allocation counters describe measured branch participation and loss accounting; they are distinct from diagnostic coverage.

# Perturbation & Tests

The geometry probe constructs appended-MASK histories. The margin probe observes supplied corrupted training inputs; it does not independently perturb sequences, compare counterfactual predictions, or test order sensitivity.
